The downside is they will chase it under the stove, behind a cabinet, under the couch, and generally places that are a pain to retrieve it from. That has limited how often we get it out for them to play with it, but when we do, they are obsessed. Lots of reviews say the battery life is horrible, so I got the extra batteries, but we are still on the original. Granted, we don't leave it out all day for them (it isn't a loud toy, but when it goes underneath something and starts vibrating against it, that can be very loud).

Full disclosure: on the second or third day of having this toy, one of our cats bit down on it, causing one of the legs to come off. The legs are tiny and not a choking or digestive concern, but this made it unbalanced, causing it to go in tiny circles and not move in straight lines anymore. I was able to find Hexbugs made for kids in the toy section of a local big box store, but without the fluffy tail. This makes the bug even more likely to go underneath things, so stick with the fluffy tailed version!

Mini Human Skeleton Model for Anatomy, 17.7'' Full Body Human Skeleton Model with Movable Arms and Legs on Plastic Base for Medical Teaching Learning, Kids Learning Education Display Tool Gift Wow, is this a toy? Because it is full of problems and inaccuracies. I’d like to start with my side-by-side photo showing some of the most egregious problems.
On the right hand with a black background is how it is supposed to look, and on the left is how it actually looks.
*Spinal alignment: any human with this type of alignment has a serious medical condition. The spine is supposed to have curvature in order to support the weight properly. As you can see by the Sideview of this toy, there is minimal curvature, and what little there is would lead the person to fall backwards. This is particularly problematic along the cervical and lumbar vertebrae (neck and lower back)
*The ribcage on this silly toy flares out at the bottom in a bizzarre way that doesn’t represent normal anatomy. Likewise, there is no attempt to indicate where the bone ends and the cartilaginous attachment points begin. Our ribs are not solid bone all the way from the vertebral column to the sternum. There’s supposed to be cartilage toward the midline as the ribs approach the sternum. Even if this model can’t indicate that, there should at least have been some sort of scoring or line or something.
The radius and ulna are ridiculous. Their thickness and size are not in correct proportion with the rest of the body. Also, why is this not in anatomical position?
Then there’s the attachment from the humerus to the glenoid fossa of the scapula, which cannot be seen in the poster or in this model. That’s just not how our arms are attached at all. Like the hip joint, the shoulder is a ball and socket joint, albeit a much shallower one than the hips. The way this is attached is so misleading and terrible. I can’t even deal with it. And circling back once again to the alignment of the spine, the pelvic bowl is completely wrong. It’s supposed to tilt downward much more.
So basically this is garbage. It’s not good for art, and it’s not really good for teaching either. What a shame. It did have some things going for it, but the issues I pointed out are too significant to ignore.
The included poster is OK, and so are a few of the skull details. It gets to stars for effort and that. But it’s pretty obvious to me that whoever designed this doesn’t know their anatomy. Imagine how much better they could’ve done if they actually paid a professional to do the design before manufacturing hundreds (thousands?) of useless little skeletons.
text_fidelity_b: Mini Human Skeleton Model for Anatomy, 17.7'' Full Body Human Skeleton Model with Movable Arms and Legs on Plastic Base for Medical Teaching Learning, Kids Learning Education Display Tool Gift

The moustache fur is made of a floppy plastic, so it does move around when the figure is moved. This was probably my favorite part of the set, as I thought it added character to the Kadabra. A little piece of advice: I recommend fitting the moustache around the knob of the piece meant to secure it, putting it together upside down instead of the way the instructions show. GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa Impressive shower head at an impressive price. Let's break it down...

** IN THE BOX ** Along with the showerhead there is a small roll of teflon thread tape, rubber pipe gasket, in-pipe flow restrictor, and instructions.

** INSTALLATION ** Remove old shower head. Clean pipe threads. Apply 3 turns of pipe thread in a CLOCKWISE direction. Extend shower head extension pipe arm all the way out. If you want flow restriction, insert now, other insert pipe gasket. Attach shower head in a CLOCKWISE direction by hand until tight. Cover the plastic thread cap (nearest the pipe) with a cloth and tighten 1/4 turn with a pliers or pipe wrench using GENTLE pressure. The shower head can now be straightened by gentle turning the adjustment screw (nearest shower head) by hand. It will click. Once you have the general downward direction of the shower head placed, test for leaks. If it leaks at the pipe & shower head connection, gently tighten another 1/4 turn. Once you're ready you can position the shower head, by head, any which way you like . It will click letting you know it's locked.

** USAGE ** Turn water on to your favorite temperature and insert your glorious naked self under the shower head. Look up at the nipples. Yes, there are 90 nipples up there. Very supple nipples that can be squeezed for cleaning. With so many nipples I don't think I'm ever leaving the shower ever again. The 90 nipples provided me an even pressurized rain all over my smelly carcass.

** THOUGHTS ** The TH2.5 works like a charm. Big, even rain all over me. Just what I wanted. Installation was simple provided you have normal shower pipes and are a bit handy with some pliers. The joints articulate well with no movement once set. The joints, once set, should accommodate short and tall humans. I'm 6'1", the wild redhead is 5'7" so this head works amazingly well for both of us. Did I mention there were 90 nipples?

** POINTS OF INTEREST **
- flow is optional and NOT installed
- joints articulate with a solid 'click' and stay in place
- pipe tape and gasket are included
- cover with cloth during final tightening to avoid scratching
- gently squeeze the nipples to clean
- looks like the USS Enterprise from the side... Aye, Aye Captain!
- I just love saying the word 'nipples'
text_fidelity_b: GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Victorian Wooden Dollhouse Furniture This is a beautiful set, with the vast majority of the pieces being thoughtfully designed and thoughtfully put together. I like that each of the room sets goes together really well, so that you have a cohesive feel throughout your dollhouse without everything feeling identical.

The quality level on some of this is absolutely stunning given that it is at a reasonable price point and made for children. I really love some of the pullout drawers that are actually functional, and the upholstery on the bed and couch, chairs and Ottoman are incredible. I think my favorite piece might be the show off cabinet that has clear plastic windows, so that you can display things in the dollhouse. We have some miniature flower vases and things like that that fit perfectly.

There were a few things that came with the quality a little bit off. The toilet arrived broken, and not only was it broken, but I could tell that the way it was put together facilitated it arriving broken. The toilet seat pins were attached in a way that the toilet seat cannot close properly over the main body of the toilet, and the part that broke off, the back toilet tank, showed very cheap pressboard material underneath, which I did not expect from Melissa and Doug brand. There were a few doors, like the refrigerator, that were also put on a little bit diagonally in a way that would drive type a grown-up a bit crazy.

The vast majority of the things however appeared to be made of real wood and had a really incredible quality and design. I put them into a new dollhouse that I'm creating for fun to play with with my kids, and it's been really fun to accessorize and make everything fit into the dollhouse in a way that feels truly special.

The packaging is ready to be dressed up or wrapped as a gift. The packaging I got was a big, wide, flat cardboard box with a plain brown exterior that you lift the lid and find a bunch of brown paper wrapped furniture. If you wrapped this with wrapping paper, it would be perfect as a gift, but if given right out the box, it definitely lacks a little sparkle. That said, once anybody realizes what is inside, the excitement level of unwrapping each individual piece was kind of like Easter, or Christmas. Really incredible.

Overall I'm really pleased with this set, and so many of these special pieces seem heirloom quality and like things that we will be so happy to continue playing with or keep for grandchildren someday.

Zobmondo!! GoLo! Golf Dice Game for Families and Kids, Award-Winning Fun Game for Home or Travel, Quick to Learn, For 1+ Players, Ages 6 and Up This game is pretty simple. Each time you take the dice you'll basically be playing nine holes of golf. The dice are set up with 2 for par 3 holes, 2 for par 5, and the remaining 5 for par four holes. When you start you'll roll all 9 dice. You must keep at least one, but can reroll all the others, and you continue to reroll until you've set aside all 9 dice at which point you score the dice.

Its that simple. Lowest score over X number of holes wins (the game suggests playing 8 rounds to simulate a full 4 day golf tournament).

Fun, portable and very easy to play. It does have the downside of basically being completely random, and in someways its a variation on Yahtzee, but its well themed. If you want a good dice game for trips and don't want Yahtzee, this is a good one to choose.

You build parks and enclosures to house dinosaurs. The dinosaurs are hungry. If you can't feed them, they'll still eat - guess what? - your other dinosaurs! Very well made and lots of fun. If you don't like this game, maybe board games aren't your thing.

I look at this game as an example to understand how to make games well. I think anyone who likes board games has to give at least one Tiny Epic game a try, and this is the one I would recommend most.

Limited closet space? Desperate for something besides Monopoly, Risk, or Settlers of Catan? Like building games with dire consequences? Think dinosaurs are the least bit cool or interesting? Look no further.

My only minor criticism is that some might consider it complex with the different special dinosaurs and some of the rules about how and when to place dinos. Any board game is going to have a learning curve, and this one is small.
text_fidelity_b: Gamelyn Games Tiny Epic Dinosaurs,12+ years

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Dual Defenders Blaster As a caveat, we are a Nerf gun family. We have spent a lot of time in the basement setting up forts, donning safety glasses, and trying to nail each other with darts. So we were a little skeptical about a "copycat" gun system just as we are of Lego rip offs. But this gun had a few happy surprises, like the way the darts stick to the special target and the incredible range we were getting on the darts.

Quality - the plastic seems a little more brittle than Nerf guns, and in general, I don't feel that they are quite up to the same level of quality. However, they have stood up to a lot of firing by the boys and are still going. And the darts are rigid and seem to be holding up to the abuse better than the foam Nerf darts do.

Aim - These have fairly decent aiming and you can consistently hit the target if not the bullseye. During battles they are fairly deadly, especially since the dates have a little more zing.

Fun factor - It's up there with Nerf. We don't include them in our battles because they have a little more zing than we want. They are good for target practice although since the darts only stick to the magic targets, you are limited with what you can aim at to get a satisfying hit. The fact that this set comes with two guns is pretty key to fun. Shields are a little gimmicky, but the boys love to pop them open and closed.

Value - They are in line with the Nerf guns. We have an arsenal of Nerf and many refills of Nerf darts so we will probably not expand into the Boomco system. Also, the refills of darts are fairly expensive, but if they end up like Nerf, you should be able to shop clearances and sales to refill.

Summary - They are not bad guns, they just aren't Nerf. The boys have enjoyed playing with these, but I think that barring an amazing design on something from Boomco, we will stick with Nerf.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Dual Defenders Blaster

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3) This is one cool Mickey! In fact, he's so cool his "ice cream doesn't melt"! (one of his cheesy phrases, not mine) Seriously, this has to be one of the coolest toys ever. Not only do both of my boys(16 months and 3 3/4 years) like it, but my husband and I love him, too. Whenever we have visitors, we have to pull this Mickey out, just to show him off. Sad, but true. One day, my 11 year old nephew was over here, and he even commented that this is the "coolest Mickey ever", and his little brother has the original dancing Mickey. I'm not familiar with the other dancing Mickeys, but apparently this one has more features.

My only complaint is the batteries, which really can't be helped with the kind of toy it is. This is more of simply a warning for you than a complaint. This Mickey really sucks the power out of batteries! He takes 6 AA batteries. He does come with a set, but they will wear off REALLY quickly. I would definitely have a high quality set of batteries waiting nearby. When the batteries get low, he will keep moving, but he won't be able to do the really fancy moves, like the handstand, and leg spins. Those are my favorite, so it's disappointing when I don't get to see those. ;)

To make him dance, all you have to do is press his nose. He will only do one set of dance moves and then he will tell you if you want to see more, just press his nose. He turns off pretty quickly. I'm sure this is so he won't use up the batteries even quicker. I like that he's smart, too. When he falls over, he asks for help getting up. When you help him up, he says, Thanks, pal!". There is an on/off switch on the back of his head. I have to make use of this switch when my youngest takes a nap.

Overall, if you don't mind the big investment price and the many batteries he will require, we HIGHLY recommend this Mickey!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3)

LEGO Disney Ariel’s Storybook Adventures 43176 Creative Little Mermaid Building Kit (105 Pieces) At first glance, the Lego series of Disney Storybook Adventures looks neat. Putting a mini playset inside a book? I think it’s fitting. Aside from Ariel in this set, the other storybooks include Anna and Elsa, Belle, and Mulan.

One of the better features of the storybooks is that the entire set fits inside. So that makes it easy for kids to take them to anywhere, without the fear of losing pieces.

There’s not a lot of actual building in the set. It’s definitely geared towards play rather than assembly. The instructions are merely a double-sided poster instead of the usual instruction booklet. There are a LOT of stickers, which I’m personally never a fan of, but at least here most of the stickers don’t have to be applied perfectly straight for the set to look okay.

The set includes 3 micro-dolls, which are just a bit smaller than Lego’s mini-dolls found in the Friends sets. The micro-dolls do not have moveable arms, movable legs, and their hands are circles, so they can’t hold a lot of accessories. There are 2 versions of Princess Ariel (one with a closed-eye wink, one with a normal expression), and Prince Eric. Small versions of Sebastian and Flounder are here, too.

When first hearing about the Storybook Adventures sets, I had hoped they could make cute gifts for friends who are fans of Disney and Lego. But when I have the set in front of me, I’m just not impressed by it. The micro-dolls aren’t great and there’s not a lot of assembly (my favorite part of Lego).
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Disney Ariel’s Storybook Adventures 43176 Creative Little Mermaid Building Kit (105 Pieces)

My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.

Blue Orange Flash! Lightening Fast Party Family Dice Rolling Game Games, for 2-6 Players, Ages 7+ Flash is a simple yet fun dice game for the entire family. It consists of six sets of six dice, each distinguished by a different color, six numbered chips for scoring, a score pad with eight challenges and a small pencil, and a storage bag and instructions.

Flash is a fast game and this is one of the reasons busy parents and others will enjoy playing it so much. The object of the game is to complete each of the eight challenges faster than your opponents and what makes it move so quickly is that everyone plays at the same time, racing against each other to see who can complete the challenge the most quickly. Unlike Yahtzee and other dice games where each person plays solo while the others wait, this game offers all- out action through each challenge.

What are the challenges in Flash? Well, they are basic numbering combinations such as six of a kind, a straight, etc. It sounds like it might be difficult, but it really isn't because each individual die has a flash (lightning bolt) on one side that counts as a wildcard. All you do is throw your dice, keep the ones that you need, then pick up the other dice and throw them again and again until you meet the challenge. Whoever completes it first yells "Flash" and picks up the highest scoring chip. Everyone else keeps throwing the dice until they get the challenge correct, but they get a lower scoring chip, all the way down to the number 1 chip. Play continues through all of the challenges and the highest scoring player wins.

The simplicity of this game is one of its strongest points and kids seem to like it more than a game such as Yahtzee for several reasons. First, the speed- it's an all- out battle to see who can meet the challenge before anyone else. Second, every challenge is certain to be met, in contrast with Yahtzee where you may or may not be able to complete each of the items on the score sheet. The scoring is simpler, too, and I like that the manufacturer included a small bag in which to place the dice, chips, pencil, and scoring pad because they would eventually get lost without it.

If I had to look for something to criticize with this dice game, it would be the fact that the challenges are really not that challenging. No matter how bad your luck may be, you will be able to complete each and every challenge- usually in two minutes max. It is only a matter of time until you roll the right numbers on the dice and the wildcard flash makes each challenge that much easier to achieve.

Family game night is part of growing up and Flash is a good game to have around on those nights when you want some family entertainment and only have about 20 minutes or less to spare. It's a fun little game that most anyone will find worthwhile and worth playing.
text_fidelity_b: Blue Orange Flash! Lightening Fast Party Family Dice Rolling Game Games, for 2-6 Players, Ages 7+

Moonlite Mini Projector with 5 Classic Winnie The Pooh Stories - A New Way to Read Stories Together - 5 Digital Stories with Light Projector - Winnie The Pooh Toys and Gifts for Kids Ages 1 and Up This MOONLITE STORYBOOK PROJECTOR (Special Edition Disney Gift Pack, for Ages 1 and Up) is a flawed concept. The projector is difficult to position over the flashlight on my Galaxy S10 phone, unless I turn the phone over and look through the lens at the light. This burns an image into my retina, and is clearly not good for my eyes!

The projector clips onto the phone, and exerts moderate pressure on the screen. I don’t like this, because I worry about cracking the screen.

The projector works with the free “Moonlite” app (available from the App Store or Google Play). You will have to register for an account to use the app. After that, you must activate each set of story reels by entering an activation code--the code is on a small card packed in the box. You tap the “unlock” icon at the top left of the app, and enter the code.

Once you’ve activated the story reel set, you click on the story you want. The app will then display a story for you to read to your child. As you read each page, you advance the reel in the Moonlite projector, to get a new illustration for each page of the story.

The projector shows a focused illustration (focus is adjustable), as long as you are no more than a yard or so away from the surface you are projecting to. You cannot project the picture across a room, or for any great distance, because the phone’s flashlight isn’t bright enough to project for long distances.

The photos that accompany the stories in the Disney set are boring, as are the stories. Kids will no doubt love the Disney characters in the pictures (e.g., Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Goofy), but the story illustrations are repetitious. Also the detail in the illustrations gets lost because the projected images are fairly small.
text_fidelity_b: Moonlite Mini Projector with 5 Classic Winnie The Pooh Stories - A New Way to Read Stories Together - 5 Digital Stories with Light Projector - Winnie The Pooh Toys and Gifts for Kids Ages 1 and Up

Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women I could not tell exactly how these “puzzles” work, even after looking at the video. You have to do two different things. First you have to “flip” each of the circles back-and-forth until you get all of them flipped to the correct side. Then you have to “spin” each of the circles to align them correctly. I find that it’s best to start from the outside circle and work your way in. The “puzzles” with most similar colors / designs on each side are the most challenging to work to get the circles on the correct side.

FYI. . . Once you have completed one side, the opposite side will not be complete. So though you will not have to flip the circles. . You’ll have to rotate the circles to complete the puzzle. So you’ll always have one side complete, and one size incomplete.

It should be noted that this “puzzle” is sturdy enough for a puzzle such as this, but it can certainly be pulled apart and broken without too much effort.

I think this “puzzle” to be best for ages tweens and up. It’s not super challenging, but again the ones with the common colors on both sides are the most challenging.

This puzzle is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon.

My style is more along the lines of giving them art supplies and letting them create what they want, and honestly, that's what I'll always prefer for them. They really enjoy projects that have a somewhat defined end result sometimes, though, and so it's kits like this that come to my rescue. Thankfully, they still get to be a bit creative with these projects, and while end results might look similar for many children, they probably won't look just alike.

There are 16 projects within this box, with lots and lots of little pieces. The supplies are all separated into different bags, and there are even extra bags for me to divide out some of the supplies. I could turn my children loose with everything and see what they come up with, but I prefer separating each project(at least for the most part), so that my children can choose which one they want to do, and not worry about running out of supplies before all the project are finished. Between my 3 children, I'll get 5 rainy days out of this box, with one extra. (I can't beat that!) ;) Plus, the included finger crayons can be used after all the projects are finished.

This is a really nice box of crafts. Especially if you're like me, and don't do so well with organized crafts, this is an excellent way to give your children some fun with crafts.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Jurassic World Jurassic Park: T. rex Rampage 75936 Building Kit (3120 Pieces) At first glance, the Lego Jurassic World T. Rex Rampage is an impressive set. It’s geared towards older builders (16+), but I would say anyone could handle it.

The set has a lot of bags and 2 thick instruction books. The first book builds the T. Rex, the second book builds the Jurassic Park gate/scenes. There’s also a sticker sheet, which I was quite disappointed to see. In a set this pricey, Lego really should have printed a Jurassic Park tile. The sticker is the main focal point on the front of the gate, so if it’s not applied perfectly, it just doesn’t look great. Lego printed a similar size tile for an Ideas set, so I don’t think it’s too crazy to suggest they should have done it for Jurassic Park!

I also wish Lego had considered how the set would be displayed. Yes, you can play with this set, but I am sure most older builders like me are building it to show it off. I personally think the scene vignettes on the *back* of the gate are cooler than the front of the gate. At least they did think of the buildable stand for the minifigs, that’s a nice touch.

By the way, the minifigures are amazing. Great detail and major thumbs up on them.

The T. Rex was my favorite part of building the set. I knew how big he was going to be since measurements are included, but knowing versus seeing are two different things. Many of his joints are ball and socket, so he can be posed in a variety of ways. But at the same time, due to the weight of his various parts, he doesn’t always stay in those poses. For example, his head often falls forward. Small parts like his toe claws fall off easily, so watch if he’s played with. I had his head and tail come off multiple times when I was trying to pose him for display. He’s delicate.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Jurassic World Jurassic Park: T. rex Rampage 75936 Building Kit (3120 Pieces)

Littlest Pet Shop Fairies Fairy Fun Rollercoaster Playset Littlest Pet Shop Fairy Fun Roller Coaster Set is a girl's toy featuring the Littlest Pet Shop characters. It is a colorful, cute toy that offers action without the need to purchase batteries. The operation is mechanical so kids can play as long as they want without the worry of batteries dying out.

This toy is nice for many reasons and besides the lack of batteries, the toy offers some simple operation and continuous action. All your girl has to do is press the lever, which moves the stairs upward and slowly transfers the small figures and their vehicles to the top of the slide where they glide around and wind up back at the base of the stairs. If you continue to press the lever, it will gradually pick up the next Littlest Pet Shop figure and send it up the stairs to the top of the slide where it will, once again, make its way around the slide to the base of the stairs.

My girls like this toy and both they and I find it to our liking. If I had to find some type of fault, it would be the tendency for the small vehicles to sometimes get out of place when they reach the base of the stairs. I haven't witnessed any problems with the vehicles gliding smoothly down the slide- the only problem I notice is that the little vehicles will sometimes get out of place at the stairs, requiring some manual assistance to re- position them. This is most likely to happen if kids get carried away and move the lever too quickly. Keep the speed at a moderate to slow rate, and there shouldn't be any problem.

Mechanical toys are nice and even though the Fairly Fun Roller Coaster Set has little or no educational value, it is still a nice toy for girls in the target age group. It is cute, colorful, and provides hours of simple amusement without the need to purchase batteries.
